title: Rib cage enclosed volume at RV, FRC, TLC, standing

quantity.name: rib cage volume
quantity.definition: volume enclosed by a closed surface mesh through all ribs

source.authors: Vergari C, Skalli W, Clavel L, Demuynck M, Valentin R, Sandoz B, Similowski T, Attali V
source.sample: 47 healthy adults (21 F, 26 M) + 11 OSAS patients (7 M, 4 F); healthy volunteers with normal pulmonary function, no musculoskeletal/respiratory/neurological history

protocol.summary: Volume enclosed by the reconstructed rib cage.
how_to_use: Check that a standing rib-cage model inflated from FRC to TLC increases enclosed volume by ~3 L (median 7.8 -> 10.9 L) while RV is close to FRC.
Do not equate with lung volume: the diaphragm contributes much of the vital capacity.

measurement.device: EOS low-dose slot-scanning biplanar X-ray; 3D reconstruction of T1-L5, ribs 1-10 and acetabula (statistical model + manual adjustment)
measurement.posture: free-standing, elbows fully flexed, fingers on cheekbones
measurement.task: acquisitions at FRC (normal breathing, reference), RV (full exhalation apnea) and TLC (full inhalation apnea), spirometer-checked

protocol.notes: TLC significantly higher (p=0.035); RV vs FRC similar. n for this analysis not stated separately (assumed healthy cohort).

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
